scores.evidence: Verified at HEAD 1aaa560. Strong structure: docs/README.md gives every document a status (current/frozen/historical/superseded), reading order per audience (lines 17-22) and a 'Known discrepancies in historical records' section (lines 91-115) that explains the $4.29/$3.55, 40- vs 50-person, harness-commit and shadow-only drift instead of editing history. README.md lines 41-52 is a measured-vs-assumed ledger with sources and routing-era labels; the 984 820 = 533 641 + 451 179 token split checks. CLAUDE.md (lines 13-39) is current after Tiers 5-8: it lists the Tier 5-7 and Tier 8 modules, templates, config files, fixtures and runs. AGENTS.md is a clean pointer. The test figure '948 passed, 7 skipped, 48 xfailed' in README.md:194, CLAUDE.md:18, TIERS.md:140 and runs/tier_8_report.md:83 matches my own run (`pytest -q`: 948 passed, 7 skipped, 48 xfailed in 11.5 s). CLI flags in docs/pilot/PILOT_RUNBOOK.md match pipeline/intake.py (--data-class, --approval-ref, --approved-by, --approved-on), pipeline/agency.py and pipeline/delivery.py (--solo-rehearsal, --actor) and pipeline/release_control.py (verify-log). runs/routing-validate-01 is tracked and README/COST_MODEL/EVAL_RECORD/docs index all label it committed. HANDOFF_WALKTHROUGH.md was moved to docs/history/ and has a clear superseded banner. The weaknesses are internal contradictions left behind by the round-1 sweep (see defects), which is exactly what this aspect judges.
defects: docs/TIERS.md:6-8 status banner says 'Tiers 0-7 are complete' and 'No Tier 8 is authorised; the owner's whole-project review loop ... is not a tier', while the same file's line 117 opens '## Tier 8 — Round 1 ...' with a green DoD, and README.md:81, docs/README.md:43, runs/tier_8_report.md and the commit subject 'tier-8: ...' all treat Tier 8 as a tier. The tier plan contradicts itself on its first screen.

runs/tier_8_report.md:3-4 still reads 'Branch: round1-integration · ... (not committed by the integrator; the orchestrator commits)' although the report is committed on main as 1aaa560; the current tier record is stale about its own status.

WALKTHROUGH.html cites docs/COST_MODEL.md by section numbers that the round-1 rewrite moved: line 1306 and 1334 cite '§2, §6' for the subscription-usage-window point (§2 is now the Haiku-era spread, §6 the token decomposition; the point is in the preamble and §5), and the €38-40 / 210 h tile cites '§3' (now 'The current routing — measured on one source'; the capacity arithmetic is §4).

docs/pilot/PILOT_RUNBOOK.md exit-code table (lines 21-29) omits exit 3 (`pending_stage`, pipeline/runner.py:40, 766) and the `corrupt_artifact` outcome that returns exit 4 (runner.py:560); an operator who sees exit 3 has no row to route by.

CLAUDE.md:8 (critical rule 2) names the read-only file as `fixtures/answer_key.json`, a path that does not exist; the keys are `fixtures/<project>/answer_key.json` (AGENTS.md:16 gets it right as `fixtures/*/answer_key.json`).
scores.to_reach_9: Fix the TIERS.md banner and the tier-8 report header, repair the COST_MODEL section references in WALKTHROUGH.html, complete the runbook exit table and the CLAUDE.md answer-key path, then add a deterministic docs-consistency test (shared figures from one source, `§N` cross-references resolve to real headings, cited repo paths exist, no 'not committed' wording next to a tracked run) so the next sweep cannot reintroduce drift.

scores.evidence: WALKTHROUGH.html (gate `tools/walkthrough/checks.py --file WALKTHROUGH.html`: 0 failures) is a genuinely good decision paper: sheet 01 leads with the ask ('Approve a four-week pilot, with live use in week 4 conditional on the retrospective results'), sheets 03-09 walk the graded run with verbatim quotes and per-step model IDs and tokens, sheet 07 shows exactly what the human decided and who signed, sheet 08 states that answer-key isolation is 'policy, not enforced file isolation' for the July run and staged copies plus a deny rule since round 1, sheet 09 labels the creative mock-up and strikes three factual errors in the drafts, and sheet 10 separates measured from assumed (598 743 vs 295 774 transcript tokens, 210 h = (120-50)x180/60, PRD §10's €5-6k corrected to €3 990-4 200), names decision owners and deadlines, and lists limits (3/10 refusals, verified against docs/demo_timing.md:20-24; voreas 15/17 then 16/17). START_HERE.html and SHARE_ME.html carry the same story consistently, including 'What it proves / What it does not prove' and the KNOWN_DEFECTS B3 disclosure; the answer-key commit time (af1527d, 2026-07-24 00:27:26) versus run start (16:38) checks. The defects are stale or under-labelled statements inside the canonical page itself, which a hiring panel that verifies claims would find.
defects: WALKTHROUGH.html:1293 (sheet 10 'Why' tile) describes the 598 743-token current-routing leg as 'one local run not committed', while the same page's ledger (line 1327: 'runs/routing-validate-01 (committed)'), README.md:48 and docs/README.md:81 say it is committed, and it is tracked in git. The decision paper contradicts itself on the provenance of the one number behind decision 2.

WALKTHROUGH.html:733 (sheet 03 ledger) says in the present tense 'runtime agents retain Read access to its [the answer key's] containing directory', contradicting sheet 08 ('Since round 1 agents read staged copies that exclude it, under a deny rule'), README.md:34-37, docs/SECURITY.md and pipeline/agents.py:67 (HARNESS_ONLY_NAMES deny rule). The same sheet calls the source header 'the input contract the runner reads' without the data declaration that owner decision 4 made part of the contract.

WALKTHROUGH.html:533 (sheet 01 headline tile) presents '0.98 M tokens ... about 15 million [a month], the figure to hold against a plan's usage window' with no routing-era label, and line 1316 repeats 'The figure to hold against a plan's usage window'. Sheet 10 itself says capacity planning 'must use the new measurement' and the one current-routing leg ran at about 2x the graded tokens, so the headline number a sponsor is most likely to carry away is the one the paper says not to plan on.

WALKTHROUGH.html sheet 02 says the core is 'about 2 500 non-blank lines, counted across the eight pipeline modules' and the agency commands 'about 2 100 more across thirteen modules'. At HEAD those eight modules have 3 607 non-blank lines (2 544 before round 1) and the thirteen agency modules 2 399: pre-round-1 figures presented as current.

The front doors count the flow differently: WALKTHROUGH sheet 02 'Nine steps, three roles: six are AI, two are plain code, one is a person's sign-off', while START_HERE.html and SHARE_ME.html say 'Ten steps, two of them people'. A reader comparing the pages sees two different system descriptions.

The tier reports a hiring panel is pointed to for Tiers 5-7 (runs/tier_5_report.md, tier_6, tier_7) are dense engineering tables with no plain-language summary of what was proved and what stays human. tier_7 still says '50-person agency' (flagged only in docs/README.md), and nothing gives a non-engineer a one-line reading of each tier.
scores.to_reach_9: Correct the four stale or unlabelled statements in WALKTHROUGH.html (committed leg, staged-input answer-key isolation plus data declaration, era label on the 0.98 M / 15 M headline, current line counts or no counts), align the step count across WALKTHROUGH, START_HERE and SHARE_ME (via pipeline/share.py), and add a one-screen 'what each tier delivered, proved and left to people' table for non-engineers in docs/README.md. Guard all of it with a test that ties the page's figures to their source artifacts.

Add the corrected phrases to tools/walkthrough/mustkeep.json and a forbidden-phrase check ('not committed' next to routing-validate-01, 'retain Read access') to tools/walkthrough/checks.py. moves.title: Deterministic docs-consistency test
moves.rationale: Every defect found this round is drift a machine can catch: repeated figures, section references, committed/local labels, cited paths. The project already gates the walkthrough and SHARE_ME. Extending that to the documentation set turns 'truth pass' from a one-off sweep into a regression guard, which is what a specialist expects before scoring 9.
moves.concrete_changes: Add tests/test_docs_consistency.py. (a) Parse '`N passed, M skipped, K xfailed`' from README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/TIERS.md (Tier 8 line), START_HERE.html, SHARE_ME.html and WALKTHROUGH.html and assert they all equal the figures in runs/tier_8_report.md §3 (or a small docs/facts.json that the report also cites). (b) For every 'docs/X.md §N' or 'X.md §N' reference in current docs and the three HTML pages, assert a heading '## N.' exists in X. (c) For every backticked repo path in documents marked Current in docs/README.md, assert it is git-tracked or listed under 'Uncommitted runs'. (d) Assert no current document pairs a git-tracked run ID with 'not committed' or 'local'. Wire it into scripts/check.sh via pytest. It asserts only on documentation and relaxes no gate.

overall: The documentation set is well above typical for an MVP. It has a status-labelled index with audience reading orders, an explicit historical-discrepancies register, a measured-vs-assumed ledger with routing-era labels, a current CLAUDE.md, and pilot runbooks whose commands match the code. The published test figures match a fresh run (948/7/48). The decision paper is honest about what was and was not proved, what stays human, and what is asked of whom. Both aspects stop at 7 for the same reason: the round-1 truth pass left concrete contradictions inside the most-read documents. TIERS.md denies the Tier 8 that its own last section records. The canonical WALKTHROUGH calls a committed run 'not committed', describes pre-round-1 answer-key access in the present tense on one sheet while another sheet contradicts it, headlines the Haiku-era 0.98 M / 15 M figure as the planning number, quotes pre-round-1 line counts and cites moved COST_MODEL sections. Each fix is small. A docs-consistency test would keep them from recurring, which is what separates 7 from 9 here.
